newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-GERMAN COURT CONVICTS PETER GRAF FOR TAX EVASION.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GERMAN COURT CONVICTS PETER GRAF FOR TAX EVASION.

text.p: A German court on Friday sentenced tennis star Steffi Graf's father to a jail term of three years and nine months for evading 12 million marks in taxes on his daughter's income.
The court in the southwestern city of Mannheim convicted Peter Graf on six counts of tax evasion and attempted tax evasion.
Presiding judge Joachim Plass said there was no evidence Steffi Graf was actively involved in any tax evasion.
Investigators had targeted the world number one in their probe into the family finances. Plass recommended the investigations against her should now be abandoned.
The court also sentenced Joachim Eckardt, a former Graf family tax adviser, to two years and six months in jail.
Both men remain free on bail until the verdict becomes legally binding, giving them time to consider an appeal.
"Graf did not want to delegate... he wanted to keep things in his own hands," Plass said in his judgment. "He wanted to be better than renowned experts."
It was not immediately clear how long Peter Graf would have to spend in jail as he had already spent 15 months in investigative custody while the probe was taking place.
Prosecutors had argued that Graf and Eckardt concealed 19.2 million marks ($11.7 million at current exchange rates) of tax on Steffi Graf's earnings from German authorities between 1989 and 1993.

Graf's lawyer had asked for a suspended sentence, arguing that Peter Graf's own naivety, the negligence of his tax advisers and the authorities' failure to act much earlier all contributed to the situation he now faced.
